data.cultural_impact: The name Jhilmil is a beautiful and poetic name in the Hindu culture. It symbolizes the fleeting yet enchanting beauty of moonbeams or raindrops, reminding us of the transient nature of life and the ephemeral moments of joy and beauty that we should cherish. It is also a name associated with nature and the seasons, evoking a sense of freshness and renewal.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the moon is considered a powerful and auspicious symbol of fertility, growth, and renewal. The name Jhilmil therefore carries with it a spiritual significance that reminds us of the cyclical nature of life and the importance of staying in tune with the natural world. It is a name that invites us to revel in the beauty and wonder of the universe and to embrace the ever-changing landscapes of our own lives.

historical_references.reference: Jhilmil is a name of a river goddess in Hindu mythology associated with the Yamuna River. The name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'jhilam' which means 'waves' or 'moving water'.

The name Jhilmil is also mentioned in the ancient Indian literary work 'Naladamayanti' by the sage Vyasa. In the story, Jhilmil is a celestial nymph who falls in love with King Nala and helps him regain his lost kingdom and wife.
